name: An installation can say who may write a lifecycle fact, who may approve and who may take the merge slot
aliases: who may record reviewed and integrated
summary: Three per-installation booleans in deployment.private.json, absent or false meaning off. admin.py coordinator-rules status|on|off [--rule NAME] --actor OPERATOR is operator-gated, holds the config lock, writes nothing when nothing changes, refuses --rule twice, and audits the last 20 flips. lifecycle_authors: implemented, tested and the task scope only from the task's assignee (compared exactly) or a listed operator, and reviewed, integrated, deployed, live-verified, enabled, live and a release deploy only from a listed operator; 'listed' is ONE rule shared with review_workflow (the operator allowlist, or an actor of a listed operator's principal). While off the write succeeds silently; admin.py lifecycle-authors PROJECT is the read-only preview. independent_approval is rule 3, both halves: approve is refused from the author's or assignee's party (principal if the registry gives one, else the normalised name), and reviewed, integrated and merge-acquire need the CURRENT contribution approved by another party. coordinator_writes refuses approve and merge-acquire unless the actor is a listed actor of the project. The session registry is read lazily, only when a rule needs it.
